importance_ranking.reason: Structural form (flat roof vs dome vs arch vs wire rope) is visually distinct and immediately communicates product type, scale, and installation quality. Buyers use the image to identify whether the structure matches their crop and site requirement before reading any text.

Structure design, net type, shading percentage, and frame material are primary shortlisting criteria — wrong spec means wrong crop outcome or subsidy ineligibility. Buyers cannot evaluate a net house listing without these dimensions.

NHB/MIDH cost norms create a per-sq-mt benchmark that farmers actively compare across sellers. Price varies substantially with structure design, net type, and frame material — buyers discover across spec tiers, making price a primary comparison signal once structural type is identified.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per acre or per structure — creates real price comparison confusion. Per sq mt is the standard unit aligned with NHB/MIDH government scheme cost norms and must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared without unit — per sq mt vs per acre vs per structure are all used in the market. Unit ambiguity directly costs buyers money and prevents accurate comparison against government subsidy benchmarks.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in the Indian net house market — it is fragmented across regional fabricators and installers; buyers search by structure type and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Subsidy-model buyers evaluate whether the supplier is NHB/MIDH empanelled and has installation track record in their region. Company credentials matter for post-sale service and subsidy documentation but rank after spec and price shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Flat roof, arch, dome, and box-type configurations are non-interchangeable — each requires different fabrication, material quantities, and wind-load engineering, driving significant price differences per sq mt.
Shade net, insect net, hail net, and bird net serve entirely different crop protection functions and use different net materials at different price points — a buyer cannot substitute one for another.

missing_important_specs.why_important: GI pipe outer diameter (25mm / 32mm / 48mm) determines structural strength and wind-load resistance — buyers in high-wind zones and NHB/MIDH subsidy schemes specify minimum pipe diameter as a compliance criterion.

Internal working height determines crop suitability — tall crops like tomato and capsicum require a minimum gutter height of 3.5m, and buyers specify this before ordering to confirm the structure fits their cultivation plan.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Structural form (flat, dome, arch, zigzag) determines fabrication complexity and material requirements — sellers need this to confirm they can supply the configuration and to price accurately.
GI pipe, wire-based, bamboo, and steel angle represent entirely different supply chains — sellers need this to confirm manufacturing capability and quote the correct material cost.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The functional purpose of the net house (shade, insect exclusion, hail protection, bird exclusion) is the most fundamental buyer requirement — it determines net specification, mesh size, and shade percentage, and sellers cannot respond accurately without it.
